1. Present revision petition is directed against an order dated 11.03.2024 passed by Ld. MM Mahila Court 2 North West Rohini, in case FIR no. 71/2019 PS Bharat Nagar, discharging the respondents/accused persons from offence u/S 406 IPC and respondent no.3/accused Tajinder Singh from offence u/S 498A IPC.

entities.text: MM Mahila Court 2 North West Rohini
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Brief facts, necessary for disposal of petition are that on 10.10.2017 the petitioner/complainant filed a complaint before CAW Cell Rani Bagh alleging cruelty against her in laws.

Before the CAW cell the mediation failed, therefore, on the recommendation of CAW cell, on 17.02.2019 the FIR was registered for offence u/S 498A/406/34 IPC and after completing the investigation all the respondents were chargesheeted for offence u/S 498A/406/34 IPC.
C.R. No. 27/2025 Ramneek Kaur Vs.
Paramjeet Singh Batra Page no. 2 of 6

. Ld. Trail Court vide impugned order held that there are no specific allegations of cruelty committed by R3 therefore charge under section 498A IPC is not made out against R3 and also held that in the entire chargesheet there is no material showing that complainant has entrusted any Stridhan with the respondent, which, on demand, respondent refused to return.
Therefore, dis- charged all respondents from offence under Section 406 IPC.

4. The order is assailed on the ground that Ld. Trail Court did not look into all the material in the charge sheet as there are alle- gations of cruelty against all the respondents including R3 and the Stridhan is not returned to petitioner till date.
Therefore charges are made out against all accused on all sections, includ- ing section 420 IPC and section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act.

5. Respondents, per contra, have submitted that there is no il- legality in the order of Ld. Trail Court as the observations of Ld. Trial Court are factual, hence the revision is liable to be dis- missed.

sentences.text: 6. I have perused the chargesheet.

7. As per Section 239 Cr.P.C., if, upon considering the police report and the documents sent with it under Section 173 and making such examination, if any, of the accused as the Magistrate thinks fit necessary and after giving the prosecution and accused an opportunity of being heard, the Magistrate considers the C.R. No. 27/2025 Ramneek Kaur Vs. Paramjeet Singh Batra Page no. 3 of 6 VIKRAM 2025.05.07 charge against the accused to be groundless, he shall discharge accused, and record his reasons for doing so.

entities.text: Ramneek Kaur Vs. Paramjeet Singh Batra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 8. It is settled position that at the stage of framing of charge Magistrate is not supposed to act as mouth piece of prosecution and to ascertain whether any charge is made out or not Magis- trate can sift and weigh the material produced in the charge sheet.
(see Sachin Kumar Vs. CBI 2010 9 SCC 368 & Union of India Vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal & Anr. 1979 SCR (2) 229).

entities.text: Union of India Vs. Prafulla Kumar Samal & Anr. 1979 SCR (2) 229
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. In the TCR, the complaint filed by petitioner is a hand written complaint in which complainant has stated that her hus- band has been cheating her since marriage as husband used to withdraw all the money from her account and he used to borrow money from others but gives her number to the creditors.
Due to which the creditors used to ask the complainant for return of money and threaten her.
When complainant discussed about the same with other accused they asked the complainant to remain silent.
However the husband did not mend his ways and kept on cheating the complainant.
Because of debts, the husband even tried to sell the gold of complainant.
She has also alleged that husband had cheated others also and whenever she confronted she was abused and beaten and he even tried to strangulate her.

She has narrated about the incident of 26.09.2017 when the com- plainant confronted her husband for cheating her sister in law as the husband has taken Rs. 1 lacs on false grounds, the husband started quarreling with the complainant and father in law also C.R. No.
27/2025 Ramneek Kaur Vs. Paramjeet Singh Batra Page no. 4 of 6 VIKRAM 2025.05.07 joined the husband and both of them asked the complainant to leave the house.

entities.text: Ramneek Kaur Vs. Paramjeet Singh Batra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On that day, complainant called her mother and her brother, after which the quarrel escalated and all three respon- dents started quarrelling with the complainant and her parents.
Therefore, complainant, in the state of confusion, finding no other option consumed phenol, however, her mother and brother intervened and threw the bottle away.
After which police was called for help but the husband in order to threaten them also consumed phenol.
Therefore, both complainant and her husband/R-1 were taken to BJRM Hospital.

10. The charge sheet also reveals that for the incident dated 26.09.2017 PCR call was made but no action was taken on that PCR call and since then complainant has been making com- plaints of physical and mental torture against her husband. There- after, when proceedings before CAW cell were conducted, the complainant further alleged about the cruelty.
11.

However, as rightly observed by ld. Trial court, there is no specific allegation against R-3 of any misbehavior with the com- plainant, except of the quarrel dated 26.09.2017, which escalated because of arrival of mother and brother of complainant.

sentences.text:
Similarly with respect to allegations of Section 406 IPC only thing complainant had stated is that her Stridhan is lying at matrimonial house but there is no allegation if Stridhan was given in custody of any of the respondent or ever demanded back C.R. No. 27/2025 Ramneek Kaur Vs. Paramjeet Singh Batra Page no. 5 of 6 VIKRAM Date:
from them.

entities.text: Ramneek Kaur Vs. Paramjeet Singh Batra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note here that the articles mentioned in the list of belongings filed by complainant, except for the per- sonal articles of complainant, no other article can be considered Stridhan as they were given at the time of marriage for common use or as gift.

13. To the personal articles of the complainant, as mentioned in the list, as there is no specific averment that these articles are entrusted with the respondent, the charge under Section 406 IPC does not lie against the applicant.
Therefore, I do not find any illegality or irregularity in the order of ld. Trial Court.
14. Revision petition is accordingly dismissed.
Copy of this judgment be sent to ld. Trial Court alongwith TCR.
